Error Signal Based Method for Real Time Pitch Extraction from Noisy Speech
abstract: <jats:p>Pitch estimation efficiency always gets affected by two major phenomena. The first one is additive noise which by nature are not correlated with the source speech signal. The second one is the vocal tract effect which creates unnecessary peaks within the signal waveform, resulting inaccurate detection of the pitch value. This paper proposes a Modified Weighted Autocorrelation Function (MWAF) executed in the Linear Predictive Coding (LPC) residual domain, instead of directly executing over the noisy source speech signal. Converting the noisy source speech signal to LP residual helps eliminating the vocal tract effects and emphasizing the necessary effects of glottal excitation. The Autocorrelation Function (ACF) and the Circular Average Magnitude Difference Function (CAMDF) are directly applied on this residual. The proposed MWAF is then calculated by multiplying the ACF with the reciprocal of the CAMDF, which enhances the periodic components as well as reduces the noise induced false peaks. Experimental results were evaluated on the KEELE and NTT databases across White, Babble, Train and HF Channel noise conditions. The result shows that our proposed algorithm reduces the Gross Pitch Error (GPE) by an average of 40.34% compared to baseline methods such as BaNa, PEFAC and WAF. Furthermore, the algorithm achieves an overall computational gain of 53.44% compared to BaNa, PEFAC and WAF, offering a stable solution for pitch tracking in degraded acoustic conditions.</jats:p>

title: HARDWARE-SOFTWARE PROTOTYPE OF A VOICE NAVIGATION SUBSYSTEM IN NOISY ENVIRONMENTS
abstract: <jats:p>The work is devoted to the development of the hardware-software prototype of a voice navigation subsystem intended for assistive navigation under acoustic interference. The relevance of the topic is explained by the need to improve the accuracy of generating voice or haptic prompts regarding the recommended route for visually impaired users based on their voice-based destination requests. The accuracy of the recommended route depends on the accuracy of voice command recognition in noisy and crowded environments. The goal of this paper is to develop a hardware-software module for voice navigation within an assistive system that enables user positioning and command recognition in the presence of acoustic interference, with the goal of enhancing the independence and mobility of individuals with visual and/or musculoskeletal impairments. The subject of this study is the processes and methods for improving the accuracy and robustness of voice command recognition in a hardware-software navigation subsystem in the presence of stationary and non-stationary noise and a multi-voice acoustic environment. The task of this work is to develop a functional model of the voice navigation hardware-software module, to develop a comprehensive sound processing algorithm that accounts for various types of acoustic interference and voice overlap; to analyze the impact of various types of acoustic interference and voice overlap on the performance of the software-hardware system. Methods such as comparative analysis, experimental models, acoustic signal recognition were applied. The results demonstrate that the proposed preprocessing and speaker-oriented filtering improve speech command recognition quality in all considered cases. WER decreased from 15.4% to 13.2% in reference conditions, from 48.6% to 30.9% under non-stationary noise, from 68.7% to 15.4% under 50 dB stationary noise, and from 73.0% to 35.3% for overlapping speech of equal loudness. The obtained results confirm the practical suitability of the proposed subsystem for assistive navigation systems operating in acoustically challenging real-world environments. Further research will focus on integrating intelligent personalization techniques into navigation feedback.</jats:p>

A Systematic Benchmark of Quantum Support Vector Machines for Interpretable Attribution of AI-Generated Text
abstract: <jats:p>Reliable attribution of artificial intelligence (AI)-generated text to a specific large language model (LLM) matters increasingly as LLMs proliferate, yet where quantum machine learning actually stands on this task has, to our knowledge, never been measured systematically. We benchmark the quantum support vector machine (QSVM) for binary attribution between Gemma 3 and Qwen 2.5 on a 5800-sample corpus from paired prompts: 83 configurations sweeping qubit count, regularization, training-set size, feature-map family, and circuit depth under exact, noiseless classical statevector simulation. QSVM validation accuracy plateaus at approximately 88%, whereas a classical support vector machine with a radial basis function kernel reaches approximately 97.8% on the identical fourteen-dimensional inputs: the ceiling belongs to the quantum (fidelity) kernel, not to the input representation. We measure the mechanism: off-diagonal quantum kernel values shrink exponentially with qubit count, the signature of exponential kernel concentration. The same classical model recovers the stylometric attribution fingerprint, showing it belongs to the shared feature pipeline rather than to the quantum kernel. All large-scale headline results generalize to an independent 1000-text test set produced after every design decision was frozen. The study provides a cautionary, reproducible benchmark for quantum kernel natural language processing and outlines an open-set extension as future work.</jats:p>

title: Decomposing the schema: reliable structured information extraction with large language models
abstract: <jats:p>Information extraction, converting unstructured text into structured data, has been reshaped by large language models: instead of labelling spans with a fixed type inventory, a single model now populates an entire predefined schema. We study this modern form, structured information extraction, among the most heavily deployed uses of these models. The default one-shot method puts the whole schema and document in one prompt and requests the entire object at once; it is fundamentally fragile, degrading silently or catastrophically as the schema grows denser, the document longer, or the model weaker. We instead decompose the schema itself into independently extractable units, query each unit separately against the document, and reassemble the outputs with a deterministic, schema-validated composer. A unit is a single field when fields are independent; when a list’s records are interdependent and unbounded in number, the entire list is one unit. Reliability matters most where it is hardest to achieve: privacy rules forbid sending the most sensitive documents to hosted frontier models, forcing extraction onto local open-weight models, precisely the weaker models on which one-shot most often fails. We evaluate on a purpose-built, fully released benchmark (800 documents across legal and medical schemas in English and Arabic, constructed ground-truth-first) over 30 open-weight models spanning four families (Qwen, Llama, Gemma, gpt-oss) and three architecture types (dense, Mixture-of-Experts, Matformer). Decomposition lifts value-accuracy macro-F1 over one-shot on every model and recovers cases where one-shot collapses entirely, including models that produce no usable output on most documents.</jats:p>

One of the problems in processing online messages is the high number of noisy texts that exist in these messages. Few studies have shown that the noisy texts decreased the result of text mining activities. On the other hand, very few works have investigated on the patterns of noisy texts that are created by Malaysians. In this study, a common noisy terms list and an artificial abbreviations list were created using specific rules and were utilized to select candidates of correct words for a noisy term. Later, the correct term was selected based on a bi-gram words index. The experiments used online messages that were created by the Malaysians. The result shows that normalization of noisy texts using artificial abbreviations list compliments the use of common noisy texts list.

abstract: <jats:p>With the surge of process modernization and enhanced data management, the world is advancing towards digitization and automation more than was presumed. The Internet is becoming one of the most favored means of communication and multimedia, coupled with data compression methods, plays a crucial role in controlling the huge volume of data that is being produced on a regular basis. Modeling novel methods for the automatic analysis of compressed data without decompression is pressing requirement of the hour. In this work a deep learning method called Linear Activated Cosine Deep Neural Network based text feature extraction from Fuzzy Filter (LACDNN-FF) quality improved compressed image documents is proposed. The LACDNN-FF method is modeled using an agent AI model. To be more specific, three different agent AIs, namely the Image Enhancement Agent (IEA), Layout Analysis Agent (LAA) and Text Feature Extraction Agent (TFEA) are employed in the design of the LACDNN-FF method. Initially, with the scanned image dataset of compressed image documents as input, two dimensional flexible fuzzy filter-based pre-processing is applied by the IEA with the intent of eliminating noise, thereby generating quality-enhanced compressed documents. Next, Linear Activated Discriminant Analysis with Deep Neural Network-based Segmentation is applied by the LAA to perform document segmentation and classify the contents using pixel-precise semantic segmentation. Finally, Cosine CNN-BiLSTM (Convolutional Neural Network - Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory) neural network based Text Feature Extraction is applied by TFEA for accurate text extraction and text feature processing. The proposed deep learning method LACDNN-FF outperforms existing methods and shows a promising solution for accurate text feature extraction with minimal error rate.</jats:p>

Bibliographic Metadata Extraction Using Deterministic Retrieval and Specialized AI Agents
abstract: <jats:p>Automated bibliographic metadata processing is a key component of intelligent library information systems. However, the use of large language models (LLMs) for bibliographic record generation is associated with factual errors, bibliographic hallucinations, and structurally incorrect metadata. This study proposes a retrieval-constrained workflow in which generative AI operates only on previously extracted and validated information from authoritative bibliographic sources. The workflow integrates deterministic metadata extraction, hierarchical source selection, normalization, multi-stage validation, and specialized AI agents for metadata structuring, Universal Decimal Classification (UDC) assignment, and MARC-formatted record generation. The architecture was evaluated on 200 real ISBN-identified bibliographic records representing 12 languages. The experimental design distinguishes ISBN-only diagnostic conditions, an external Google Books bibliographic metadata baseline, a retrieval-only internal architectural ablation, and the full specialized AI Library workflow. Google Books returned exact ISBN-matched records for 48 of the 200 submitted identifiers (24.0% coverage), resulting in a macro-average manually verified field-level accuracy of 14.8% over the complete dataset. In the controlled GPT-4o comparison, the specialized AI Library workflow increased the macro-average manually verified accuracy of the principal bibliographic fields from 65.0% to 83.2%. It also increased the UDC Recognition Rate from 85.0% to 99.5% and COMARC/B record-generation coverage from 87.5% to 97.5%, while mean Exact+Partial correspondence with the COBISS reference records increased from 62.1% to 73.6%. Overall, the results demonstrate consistent improvements in bibliographic metadata accuracy, UDC assignment coverage, and COMARC/B record-level correspondence.</jats:p>

title: Research on adaptive signal detection and feature extraction method of complex electronic information system
abstract: <jats:p>Aiming at the challenge of signal detection and feature extraction in complex electromagnetic environment, this paper proposes an adaptive joint optimization method of signal detection and feature. Faced with the problems of traditional methods relying on prior knowledge, insufficient deep learning generalization ability, and poor adaptability to non-stationary noise, a cascaded framework was constructed that includes variable step size LMS (VSS-LMS) interference suppression, multi head self-attention (MHSA) feature extraction, and dynamic threshold decision-making. VSS-LMS achieves fast convergence and steady-state error balance by improving the tongue line function. MHSA uses multi-scale attention mechanism to focus on the characteristics of target signal adaptively. Adaptive threshold dynamically adjusts the threshold based on local noise power estimation. Experiments show that the detection probability of this method is 96% in the signal-to-noise ratio range of -15 dB to 5 dB, which is more than 15% higher than that of the traditional method. The accuracy of feature classification is over 94.3%, and the false alarm probability is stable below 0.01. The three modules cooperate to improve the detection sensitivity and feature discrimination in dynamic electromagnetic environment, and provide a new scheme for intelligent perception of complex electronic information systems.</jats:p>

Evaluating Vision-Language Models for Structured Information Extraction from Heterogeneous Multi-Page Laboratory Reports
abstract: Background Laboratory reports vary widely in layout, length, and scan quality, making automated data extraction difficult. While vision-language models (VLMs) handle both visual and textual inputs, it is not fully understood how document-processing granularity affects their extraction accuracy. Objective We evaluated how model choice, document length, and processing strategy affect VLM performance and efficiency when extracting structured data from multi-page clinical reports. Methods We designed a controlled experiment using de-identified laboratory reports from Lal PathLabs and Thyrocare. We tested short (1 page), medium (5–6 pages), and long (10 pages) documents in both digital and scanned formats. Testing three workflows—Qwen2.5-VL complete-report, Qwen2.5-VL page-wise, and Llama 3.2 Vision page-wise—resulted in 36 experimental runs covering 1,080 expected test occurrences. We compared the extracted records to a manual ground truth, measuring precision, recall, F1-score, overall accuracy, and processing time. Results Qwen2.5-VL processed page-by-page achieved the highest overall accuracy (98.89%), recall (98.89%), and F1-score (97.80%). This method remained stable even as report length increased, averaging 67.43 seconds per report. Processing the entire report at once with Qwen2.5-VL was much faster (32.08 seconds per report) and highly precise (99.71%). However, its overall accuracy dropped to 94.44% because it missed tests in longer documents. The Llama 3.2 Vision page-wise workflow recorded the lowest accuracy (87.22%) and took the longest (108.12 seconds per report), frequently generating extra, incorrect records. Conclusions The success of VLM data extraction depends heavily on how the input is chunked. Processing reports page-by-page prevents data loss in complex documents, while whole-document processing offers a clear speed advantage. Clinical pipelines should select the strategy that best matches their specific speed and accuracy requirements.

abstract: <jats:p>Educational institutions and professionals must analyze student performance to identify ways to improve each student's academic achievement. Predicting how well students will do in universities and colleges is crucial for managing their time effectively. Predicting students' academic achievement has been the subject of some relevant research activity since the advent of deep learning. Students' academic performance is affected by various factors, yet there is a general trend of similar intelligence and learning styles among students at the same university. The goal of this research is to use deep learning algorithm and historical data to forecast how well students will do in academics. Academic performance analysis can be enhanced by combining a Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer (T5) with a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) model. This allows us to leverage the capabilities of both architectures. In contrast to Bi-LSTM's adeptness at capturing sequential dependencies, T5's text-to-text method offers a versatile framework for encoding and processing a wide range of academic data. Accuracy in activities such as requirements classification and short response grading can be enhanced using this hybrid technique. The proposed T5-BiLSTM model is used to accurately identify the predictive variables from academic datasets that majorly influence the academic performance. This research is helpful for educational institutions to identify the predictive variables that are used to enhance the student academic progress.</jats:p>

title: Explainable Clinical Text Mining for Treatment Response Extraction in Lung Cancer Notes
abstract: <jats:p>The extraction of treatment response information from unstructured clinical notes is a critical task in oncology research and clinical practice, particularly for lung cancer, where therapeutic paradigms evolve rapidly. Despite the promising capabilities of advanced natural language processing models, their opaque nature significantly limits clinical adoption due to a lack of interpretability and trustworthiness. This paper investigates the development and implementation of an explainable clinical text mining framework explicitly designed to extract treatment response trajectories from unstructured electronic health records pertaining to lung cancer cohorts. By integrating transformer-based language models with robust explainability techniques, the proposed methodology aims to bridge the gap between high predictive performance and clinical transparency. The analysis encompasses an exhaustive review of current natural language processing applications in oncology, a detailed explication of the architectural design prioritizing attention-based interpretability, and a rigorous evaluation against traditional black-box methodologies. The findings demonstrate that augmenting extraction models with explanatory mechanisms not only maintains state-of-the-art accuracy but also significantly enhances clinician trust by providing verifiable linguistic evidence for every automated extraction. This research underscores the necessity of transparent artificial intelligence in high-stakes medical domains and provides a scalable blueprint for deploying explainable text mining systems in real-world oncology workflows.</jats:p>

title: Text Mining and Machine Learning for New-MediaPublic-Opinion Spillovers in Manufacturing Supply-Chain Digital Collaboration
abstract: <jats:p>Online media coverage may transmit information across supply-chain relationships, yet converting such signals into evidence requires a clear separation between text measurement, network alignment, and statistical inference. This study examines whether focal-firm media attention is associated with connected partners’ annual-report digital disclosure and develops a manufacturing-oriented workflow for directed supply-chain analysis. We construct a firm–partner–year panel for Chinese non-financial A-share firms from 2007 to 2024 by combining aggregated CFND media indicators, annual-report digital-term frequencies, CNRDS supplier–customer links, and CSMAR controls. Fixed-effects models estimate conditional associations on directed edges. The baseline specification shows a positive association between focal-firm coverage and partner digital disclosure (β = 0.048, SE = 0.020), while alternative aggregate coverage measures yield coefficients with the same sign; mechanism and subgroup results remain observational and descriptive. These findings do not establish causality or realized interfirm digital collaboration because annual-report word frequency is an imperfect disclosure proxy. A Chinese- BERT–MLP event-and-tone module is therefore retained only as a future extension pending article-level text, human- reviewed labels, and out-of-sample evaluation.</jats:p>

title: Multiple-InstanceLearning in Medical Imaging: Correlated Chained Gaussian Processes with a Weighted Noisy-OR Likelihood
abstract: <jats:p>Whole-slide images and computed tomography scans are commonly decomposed into patches or slices, whereas diagnostic labels are assigned only at the study level, so that which patches or slices support the diagnosis remains unknown. Multiple-instance learning addresses this weakly supervised setting through aggregation functions, which determine how instance-level evidence produces the bag-level prediction. Several probabilistic MIL methods rely on max-based aggregation, which retains only the strongest instance evidence. On the other hand, the standard noisy-OR combines all instance scores, so that the bag probability depends on the product between the bag cardinality and the average instance activation. As a consequence, a slide covered by thousands of benign patches can receive the same probability as one containing a small tumor region. We introduce Correlated Chained Gaussian Processes with Weighted Noisy-OR Likelihood (CCGP-WNOR), a framework in which each instance is assigned a weight that modulates its contribution to the bag probability, with the weights summing to one so that the aggregation is normalized. Consequently, the bag probability lies between the minimum and maximum instance scores, and a value close to one requires at least one instance carrying strong positive evidence. Instance scores and aggregation weights are obtained by transforming two latent functions coupled through a semiparametric latent factor model with shared Gaussian processes, permitting cross-output dependence in the prior. Posterior uncertainty is propagated through a factorized approximation that preserves marginal means and variances but omits cross-output and cross-instance covariances from likelihood integration and prediction. Scalable inference is performed using inducing variables and stochastic variational inference. Experiments on a semi-synthetic benchmark and three medical imaging datasets show that CCGP-WNOR achieves a competitive performance among the compared state-of-the-art MIL methods.</jats:p>

title: A deep learning framework for robust text extraction from heterogeneous image sources
abstract: <jats:p>Text extraction from an image is characterized by various challenges that result in various evolving solutions at current times. Existing solutions using artificial intelligence (AI) do have some promising outcomes, but also have their own shortcomings associated with accuracy and efficiency. The manuscript introduces a simplified and yet innovative AI framework towards extracting text by unifying character region-aware text detection. The model uses a convolutional neural network (CNN) along with transformer-centric optical character recognition (OCR) towards better performance on scene text recognition. Analysis is carried out on the standard and benchmarked International Conference on Document Analysis and Recognition 2015 (ICDAR 2015) dataset to find that the proposed model accomplished 94.7% accuracy and 0.82 seconds per image of response time, which are much significant improvements in performance, while observed in contrast to existing AI models, proving the model to deliver high-performance and cost-effective outcomes.</jats:p>

title: From Crash Narratives to Structured Liability and Severity: An LLM Information-Extraction Pipeline for Autonomous-Vehicle Insurance Triage
abstract: <jats:p>As autonomous-vehicle (AV) fleets scale, insurers must convert a growing volume of unstructured collision reports into the structured signals that reserving and subrogation require. Two regulatory regimes already mandate free-text crash narratives-the U.S. NHTSA Standing General Order (SGO 2021-01) and the California DMV's OL 316 collision reports-yet these narratives are largely unexploited for predictive use. We build and evaluate a schemaconstrained large-language-model (LLM) pipeline that codes these narratives into a structured representation of collision type, pre-crash maneuver, engagement state, operating-environment conditions, and a narrative-described contributory party. We evaluate it primarily against a distant-supervision key: the structured codes the reporting entities themselves file alongside each narrative, which supply 31,204 supervised field decisions across ten fields. The best model attains a median κ of 0.703 against this key, with the residual disagreement dominated by conditions the narratives simply do not state rather than by mis-extraction. We then ask whether narrative text adds predictive value for injury severity beyond the structured fields insurers already collect, using entity-grouped cross-validation and a leakage-controlled design that excludes any text-derived restatement of the outcome. Adding text yields a quadratic-weighted-κ lift of 0.180 over the structured-only baseline.</jats:p>

title: A Text Classification Method for Telecom Fraud Based on Fusion of TF-IDF Feature Extraction and BERT Model
Affordances Without a Body: How Text-Only Large Language Models Represent and Use Affordance-Related Information
abstract: <jats:p>Text-only Large Language Models (LLMs) lack direct sensorimotor experience, yet they are trained on language produced by embodied agents. This raises the embodiment problem of whether language can transmit enough regularities about body–world interaction for a disembodied model to reconstruct action-related information. Affordances provide a particularly stringent test case, since by definition they concern action possibilities that depend on the current state of an object or environment. Rather than asking whether LLMs simply ”possess” affordances in a Gibsonian sense, we investigate how text-only LLMs rep-resent and use affordance-related information. We introduce an experimental framework that distinguishes three levels of affordance-related processing (latent representational accessibility, context-sensitive behavioral use, and their association), together with a fourth analysis probing generalization to a finer affordance distinction. Applying it to three architectures (GPT-OSS-20B, Qwen3.5-27B, and Gemma-4-31B-it) through probing, geometric, and behavioral analyses, we find that affordance information is consistently linearly decodable and organized along coherent latent directions, though the categories do not form fully separated clusters. In some architectures, stronger latent affordance representations are further associated with greater contextual behavioral sensitivity. The overall pattern is graded and architecture-dependent rather than all-or-none, suggesting that linguistic experience can reconstruct some action-related regularities without providing evidence of genuine sensorimotor grounding or embodied cognition.</jats:p>

title: XBRIDGE: Cross-Domain Bridge Distillation for Data-Efficient Video Classification
abstract: <jats:p>Compact video classifiers often underfit on small, domain-specific datasets, while mismatched pretraining sources can limit direct knowledge distillation. We propose Cross-Domain Bridge Distillation (XBRIDGE), which transfers knowledge from a teacher through an assistant pretrained on a semantically adjacent video domain to a compact student. On XD-Violence, a Kinetics-400 assistant achieves higher standalone accuracy (86.26%) but produces a weaker student (68.39%) than a cross-domain Something-Something V2 assistant (72.95%). This suggests that assistant accuracy is a poor proxy for transfer quality and motivates investigating temporal and object-interaction priors for low-data targets. A lightweight Contextual Bridge Optimiser supports assistant and supervision-weight selection under a fixed compute budget. Evaluation on binary violence detection and multiclass sports recognition shows gains over direct fine-tuning and direct distillation. We report parameters, FLOPs, and latency alongside classification performance to characterise the trade-offs for compact video transformers.</jats:p>

Improving Parameter-Efficient Medical Image Classification with Lesion-Aware Hierarchical Knowledge Distillation
abstract: <jats:p>Compact deep models are attractive for medical image classification, but conventional knowledge distillation mainly transfers class-level predictions and may not adequately preserve lesion-relevant spatial cues. To address this limitation, we propose LaHKD, a lesion-aware hierarchical knowledge distillation framework for parameter-efficient medical image classification. LaHKD enables a lightweight student to learn hierarchical semantic representations together with lesion-focused guidance from a stronger teacher. We evaluate LaHKD on HAM10000 dermoscopic lesion classification and a brain tumor MRI classification benchmark. Across both datasets, LaHKD improves compact-student classification performance, with the clearest lesion-focused spatial benefits observed on HAM10000, where lesion morphology is central to diagnosis and direct lesion supervision is available. On the magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) benchmark, localization analysis is limited to an auxiliary recovered-mask subset and is therefore interpreted as exploratory; under this setting, consistent localization gains are not observed. Overall, LaHKD provides an effective framework for compact medical image classification, with spatial benefits most clearly supported in tasks with reliable lesion supervision.</jats:p>

Enhancing EHR Text Classification: A Hybrid BERT Hashing Framework for Interpretability, Robustness, and Data-Efficient Medical Text Classification
abstract: <jats:p>The clinical narratives contained in EHRs are long, unstructured, with dense information content, and difficult to classify due to uneven length, structure, terminology, and information density. This work presents a hybrid machine learning system that uses classifiers to classify medical transcription, focusing on data efficiency, interpretability, and robustness. The pipeline combines natural language preprocessing, Domain-informed feature extraction, Hashing Vectorizer representation and BERT representation for context. Five features identified in the original study document length, bigram type, relationship words, word count, and noun/verb counts are included to capture complementary lexical, syntactic, and domain information. The Medical Transcriptions Dataset consists of 80% training and 20% testing data. The reported evaluation includes 2321 test samples. Test-set accuracy is about 74.2%, weighted precision is about 74.4%, weighted recall is about 74.2%, and weighted F1 score is about 72.7%. The average macro F1 is around 50.0%, which shows significant class-to-class variation. Many low-support categories have low or zero F1 values, while several high-support categories have strong F1 values. After 6 epochs, the training loss drops from 0.67 to 0.46, and the reported validation F1 rises from 66% to 77% and ultimately levels off. These results show that a hybrid representation of heterogeneous medical text is feasible, but also indicate significant class imbalance and limited minority-class examples. The updated framework thus suggests balanced learning, external validation, systematic ablation, robustness testing, and clinically assessed interpretability before real-world deployment.</jats:p>

Efficient attack classification in decoy systems: an ensemble learning approach with text-based data augmentation
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Network attack decoy systems are widely deployed to lure adversaries and collect detailed attack behaviors. However, the massive and heterogeneous logs they generate, together with the imbalance between normal and attack traces, make it difficult to build reliable automatic classifiers. Motivated by these challenges, in this paper we propose an efficient attack classification decoy system to improve the automatic network attack classification capability of decoy-based defences. In this paper, we propose an efficient attack classification strategy in decoy systems, based on an ensemble learning approach with text-based data augmentation, to address these issues. To elucidate, an attack sequence generation method is proposed to simplify the logs and transform the attack classification problem into a text categorization problem. Additionally, we tackle the data imbalance issue by employing data augmentation on the extracted numerical features from the text. Moreover, we construct our classification model based on ensemble learning, utilizing various classifiers in conjunction with diverse features. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach improves accuracy and precision by over 10% in attack classification, significantly improving classification effectiveness. Furthermore, we deployed our system in a real-world environment to validate its performance. The results reveal notable accomplishments in attack deception and attack classification.</jats:p>

title: Continual Image-Text Retrieval via Banzhaf Distillation from the Coalitional Game Perspective
abstract: Continual image-text retrieval (CITR) aims to accomplish the cross-modal retrieval job in the form of sequential multimedia data instead of single entire dataset. Due to the multi-granularity and semantic misalignment of vision and language modalities, CITR exhibits three challenges: spatial disorder of cross-modal data, heterogeneous structure of semantics and hierarchy of knowledge of cross-modal data, and knowledge aliasing during incremental sessions. The key insight is that traditional CITR methods use model the token-by-token similarity, which fails to capture fine-grained semantics especially when knowledge experiences multiple modalities and different incremental sessions. From the coalitional game perspective, we observe that each pairwise tokens of images and texts can act as coalition participants, the Banzhaf valuation can be modeled to characterize multi-grained semantics of image-text pairs. Based on this idea, we propose the Banzhaf Distillation Network (BDNet) for CITR. The core component of BDNet is the Banzhaf Distillation module, which preserves the structural cross-modal knowledge with the Banzhaf value, and retains the cross-task structural knowledge with a token-level similarity closeness constraint. Essentially, the Banzhaf valuation models the high order relation of image tokens and text tokens by using their interaction with respect to other tokens towards the semantic alignment of two modalities. Extensive experiments on several single-set scenarios and multi-set scenarios demonstrate the effectiveness of BDNet under single-set and multi-set scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/wangsfan/CBD.

title: Efficient Diffusion Distillation via Embedding Loss
abstract: <jats:p>Diffusion distillation converts expensive iterative diffusion samplers into few-step or one-step generators. However, distribution-matching distillation often relies on large batches and long training schedules, which are difficult to sustain on limited hardware. We introduce Embedding Loss (EL), an online auxiliary Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) objective that compares real and generated samples in randomly initialized feature spaces. The feature extractors are resampled at every optimizer update and remain fixed during that update. EL requires neither pre-generated teacher outputs nor an adversarial discriminator. We analyze the stochastic gradient of distribution matching and separate batch-size-dependent Monte Carlo error from update-shared randomness, motivating EL as a complementary distribution-level signal. Experiments across CIFAR-10, ImageNet at 64*64 and 512*512 resolution, AFHQ-v2, and FFHQ show that EL is most beneficial when the training batch is small. It improves Fr&apos;echet Inception Distance (FID) or convergence speed when combined with distribution-matching and Consistency Distillation objectives. On CIFAR-10, direct measurements show an 8.09% reduction in relative gradient variance and an 8.80% increase in gradient signal-to-noise ratio. Resource-constrained runs reach FID values of 1.475 for unconditional and 1.380 for conditional generation. These results show that EL is a lightweight and broadly compatible auxiliary objective for improving diffusion distillation under limited computational resources.</jats:p>

title: Multistage Simultaneous Knowledge Distillation Driven Lightweight and Efficient Broad Learning System for 3-D Object Classification
Class-Structure Preservation Beats Diversity: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Text Augmentation Methods for Imbalanced Text Classification
abstract: <jats:p>With the rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs), generative data augmentation has attracted considerable attention for imbalanced text classification in natural language processing. However, no empirical benchmark to date has compared LLM-based augmentation against the embedding-space SMOTE-style retrieval (EmbSMOTE), a strong classical reference for imbalanced classification. In this study, a controlled benchmark of 11 augmentation methods, spanning classical perturbation, embedding-space retrieval, and LLM-based generation, is newly constructed on seven public text classification datasets covering class counts K=2 to 28 and imbalance ratios of 1.1 to over 500, evaluated with five random seeds per cell using macro F1, Welch&apos;s t-tests, five distributional metrics, and an LLM-family sensitivity analysis based on Qwen3-8B. The experimental results reveal that all LLM-based methods are statistically equivalent or inferior to EmbSMOTE, with the performance gap widening monotonically as imbalance increases and reaching ΔF1macro ≈ 0.063 on GoEmotions-28. Furthermore, it is observed that surface-level uniqueness has negligible correlation with downstream performance, whereas LLM-specific artifacts, such as text elongation and label-distribution uniformization, are negatively associated with classification accuracy. Compared with six LLM-based and four classical augmentation baselines, these results demonstrate that the effective variable is not surface-level diversity but class-conditional structural fidelity, namely the degree to which augmented samples preserve the class-conditioned geometry of the training distribution. Accordingly, retrieval-based oversampling should be adopted as the default for imbalanced multi-class classification, and a higher empirical bar should be required before LLM-based augmentation is deployed in practice.</jats:p>

title: An Empirical Study of Synthetic Data Augmentation for Few-Shot Text Classification Using Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Ultra-Lightweight Language Model
Multi-Teacher Contrastive Distillation for Lightweight Plant Disease Classification
abstract: <jats:p>Lightweight deep models offer a promising avenue for real-time plant-disease recognition on edge devices, yet their accuracy often degrades under stringent compute budgets. We propose CropKD, a resource-aware classification framework that synergistically integrates three neural-computing components: (i) a lightweight multi-scale feature fusion module (LMFF) that enriches spatial representation via parallel depth-wise convolutions and channel-wise attention; (ii) a multi-teacher adaptive distillation strategy (MTAD) that dynamically fuses complementary knowledge from convolutional and vision-transformer teachers; and (iii) a contrastive knowledge distillation loss (CKD) that tightens intra-class embeddings while enlarging inter-class margins. Extensive experiments on FGVC8, BARI-Sunflower and DiaMOS show that CropKD achieves state-of-the-art accuracies of 94.5\%, 98.99\% and 94.11\%, respectively, while retaining only 4.5 M parameters, 0.6 GFLOPs, 2.8 GB RAM and 95 W power. On a Jetson Nano it runs at 36 FPS, demonstrating real-time deployability under true field conditions. The results validate CropKD as a generic recipe for compressing heavy vision transformers into ultra-light edge-intelligence models, and provide a practical tool for sustainable smart agriculture. Code, pretrained weights and splits will be made publicly available.</jats:p>

title: Prototype-guided semantic transferability for reliable knowledge distillation in brain tumor MRI classification
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Brain tumor classification from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains challenging due to subtle inter-class differences, imaging variability, and uncertainty in model predictions. Although deep learning models achieve strong performance, their complexity limits deployment in resource-constrained settings, making knowledge distillation a practical approach for transferring knowledge to lightweight student models. However, conventional distillation methods typically assume uniform teacher reliability and often overlook semantic structure and prediction reliability. To address this limitation, we propose a prototype-guided semantic transferability framework that selectively transfers knowledge based on predictive confidence and alignment with class prototypes in an embedding space. The method introduces a prototype memory to capture class-level structure and formulates a transferability score to adaptively weight the distillation process. Experiments demonstrate consistent improvements in classification performance, calibration, robustness, and cross-dataset generalization while preserving the efficiency of the student model. Ablation studies, statistical analysis, and feature space visualizations further support the effectiveness of the proposed components. Overall, the proposed framework aims to enhance knowledge distillation by incorporating semantic structure and uncertainty, leading to more reliable and discriminative representations without additional inference overhead.</jats:p>

title: SAS Multimetric Tribunal: Structural Classification of Hallucination in AI-Generated Text
abstract:
<jats:p>Hallucinations in large language models (LLMs) remain a critical barrier to the safe deployment of AI-generated text in high-stakes domains. Existing detection methods typically rely on auxiliary LLMs, reference-based metrics, or human evaluation—approaches that are computationally expensive, opaque, and difficult to audit. This paper presents the SAS Multimetric Tribunal, a lightweight, fully interpretable structural classification system that evaluates (source, response) pairs across seven detection modules using a cascading multiplicative penalty strategy. The tribunal partitions the output space into three structural zones—Structural Collapse (F-S), Recoverable Rupture (B), and Coherent (A)—governed by two thresholds: \(\kappa_{D} = 0.56\) (coherence boundary, registered TAD EX-2026-18792778) and \(\kappa_{R} = 0.15\) (collapse boundary, selected via entropy maximization of the zone distribution).

Over an expanded benchmark of \(n = {1,800}\) pairs (600 HaluEval-Dialogue + 600 HaluEval-QA + 600 TruthfulQA), each evaluated under an A\(\rightarrow\)A sanity check and an A\(\rightarrow\)B hallucination condition, the tribunal achieves \(\text{F1} = {98.99\%}\), Precision \(= {100.00\%}\) (zero false positives under the sanity check), Recall \(= {98.00\%}\), and 36 false negatives (range across sampling seeds: F1 98.99–99.02%, FN 35–36). CRUCIALLY, WE DOCUMENT THAT 100% OF ERRORS (36/36) CONCENTRATE IN TRUTHFULQA AND EXHIBIT A PREDICTABLE STRUCTURAL PATTERN: HIGH-LEXICAL-SIMILARITY FACTUAL HALLUCINATIONS THAT TRIGGER NO SPECIALIZED MODULE, LEAVING LEXICAL_BASELINE_SCORE AS THE SOLE DISCRIMINATOR. We treat these 36 false negatives not as noise but as the _documentable failure mode_ of the current lexical baseline against stealth hallucinations.

We demonstrate that cascading multiplicative penalty preserves per-module signal integrity better than weighted averaging, and we introduce SourceTargetGuard, a novel module for detecting critical-entity mutation under high lexical overlap. We explicitly caution that the reported metrics constitute an UPPER BOUND UNDER A TAUTOLOGICAL SANITY CHECK (A\(\rightarrow\)A); the real negative control (A\(\rightarrow\)C valid paraphrase), executed in this revision, confirms a 99.2% false-positive rate on paraphrases, which we document as the primary open limitation. This revised version additionally reports a FORENSIC AUDIT OF THE METRICS PUBLISHED IN THE PREVIOUS MANUSCRIPT VERSION: we could not initially locate a validation artifact matching the previously reported numbers, re-executed the validation under a fully documented and seeded protocol, and confirm that the earlier metrics were reproducible (not fabricated) but had been insufficiently documented at the time — a distinction we consider important enough to report in full rather than silently correct. This revision integrates a systematic Known Limitations section, articulates the methodological contributions, and corrects the documentation inconsistencies identified during peer review and internal audit.</jats:p>

title: Cross‐corruption distillation for robust instruction following under text corruptions
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Traditional knowledge distillation transfers information from a large teacher model to a compact student by aligning static output distributions or internal representations for fixed inputs. Such formulations overlook how predictions change in response to input perturbations, even though robustness is critical for deployment. We interpret distillation as the transfer of functional response behavior under input variations and propose cross‐corruption distillation (CCD), which aligns corruption‐induced differences in teacher and student output via a Kullback–Leibler objective. Rather than matching absolute logits, CCD distills how the teacher redistributes its prediction mass under perturbations, transferring teacher‐conditioned input sensitivity without architectural correspondence. On diverse multimodal benchmarks, CCD performs competitively, often outperforming conventional logit‐based distillation. It also slows performance degradation as perturbation strength increases and remains stable across corruption strategies and training schedules. These results position CCD as a response‐aware distillation framework integrating robustness directly into the distillation objective.</jats:p>

HHRA: Hyperbolic Hierarchical Relation Alignment for Hierarchical Text Classification
abstract: <jats:p>Hierarchical text classification assigns labels to documents according to a predefined label taxonomy. Existing methods often rely on shared document representations and static label structures, which may cause semantic interference among labels and fail to capture instance-specific hierarchical relationships. To address these limitations, we propose HHRA, a Hyperbolic Hierarchical Relation Alignment model. HHRA learns label-specific representations by separating primary discriminative features from complementary semantic information. It then maps label-specific text representations and label semantic representations into a Lorentz hyperbolic space, where hierarchy-aware contrastive learning is performed using positive, sibling, descendant, and random labels. The resulting text-conditioned relation priors are combined with the global label hierarchy to guide hierarchical feature re-aggregation. Experiments on four benchmark datasets, WOS, RCV1-V2, BGC, and NYT, show that HHRA achieves the highest reported overall performance among the compared methods. In particular, it obtains Micro-F1 and Macro-F1 scores of 82.72 and 74.70 on NYT, respectively. Ablation studies further demonstrate the effectiveness of label-specific representation learning, hyperbolic relation alignment, and dynamic hierarchical re-aggregation. These results indicate that HHRA is particularly effective for hierarchical text classification with deep taxonomies and complex label paths.</jats:p>

title: DOR-vul: Cross-modal reasoning distillation for efficient vulnerability recognition
Cross-Modal Relation Preservation Knowledge Distillation from VLMs for Fine-Grained Visual Classification
abstract: <jats:p>Knowledge distillation has emerged as an effective approach to distill large-scale Vision-Language Models (VLMs) into lightweight networks under resource-constrained settings. However, existing VLM distillation methods typically transfer knowledge by matching output probabilities, requiring the student model to perform point-wise alignment with the teacher&apos;s predictive distribution, which may fail to fully exploit the rich relational information embedded in VLM visual-language similarities. To address this issue, we propose Cross-Modal Relational Preservation Knowledge Distillation(CMRP-KD), which directly integrates the multimodal knowledge of VLMs into a compact model during training and shifts the distillation objective from probability matching to relational structure preservation. Specifically, CMRP-KD models cross-modal relations from two complementary levels of the VLM visual-language similarity matrix, and employs Pearson correlation-based constraints to preserve the relative relational structure between the teacher and student, thereby enabling more effective transfer of cross-modal knowledge. Extensive experiments on multiple fine-grained image classification benchmarks demonstrate that CMRP-KD generally outperforms existing VLM distillation methods, improving classification accuracy while maintaining high inference efficiency without introducing any additional computational overhead during inference. The code is available at https://github.com/WMX1007/CMRP-KD.</jats:p>

How Evaluation Splits Reshape Conclusions in Short-Text Field Classification: A Case Study on Educational Data Domain Classification
abstract: <jats:p>Data classification and grading regulations require organizations to assign field-level semantic categories to structured data before sensitivity assessment, but short, context-poor field names make this nontrivial. We design and evaluate a character–word–sentence fusion architecture on a standardstraceable Chinese educational-field corpus (162 concepts drawn from seven Ministry-of-Education standards) under two evaluation protocols. Under aconventional sample-level split, character-only and word-only branches alone already approach ceiling performance (macro-F1 0.98 and 0.99), because the same concept’s naming variants recur across training and test and these fromscratch embeddings memorize surface patterns rather than learn transferable semantics. Under a concept-level held-out split, where no test-set concept’s name appears in training, the ranking reverses: over six partitions, characterand word-level branches degrade to mean macro-F1 0.38–0.39, while every combination including the pretrained sentence encoder scores substantially higher (0.51–0.56), a clean separation by whether the sentence branch is included. Enriching the input with the field’s textual explanation, intended to help weak-semantics fields, achieves a leaked perfect score under the samplelevel split but is consistently worse than the plain input under concept-level holdout, across all six partitions. A confirmatory case study on 142 real fields from a Chinese university reproduces the same leaked-perfect-score failure mode and shows that a real deployment can be too table-scarce to construct the recommended held-out check. These findings indicate that sample-level splits on field-classification corpora with repeated underlying concepts can substantially overstate generalization, and we argue that concept-level (or table-level) held-out evaluation should be reported alongside conventional splits for this task family.</jats:p>

title: Rafale: Towards the Efficient Resource-Aware Federated Knowledge Distillation on Heterogeneous Clients
abstract: <jats:p>Knowledge distillation is an highly effective machine learning technique for transferring knowledge from a large model, i.e., teacher, to a smaller model, i.e., student, improving model efficiency without sacrificing performance. This paper proposes a novel resource-aware federated learning framework Rafale that incorporates an adaptive client clustering mechanism based on computational resource availability and model complexity. High-resourceb clients train complex teacher models, and low-resource clients leverage distilled knowledge from teachers to train lightweight student models. Further, to optimize the aggregation process by introducing a clustering-based weightsharing mechanism that minimizes communication overhead while maintaining model accuracy. In this paper, a revolutionary Rafale framework that greatly reduces communication cost and separates model training from architectural constraints is proposed. To increase scalability and robustness, the suggested method makes use of resource-aware client selection, adaptive information sharing, and effective distillation techniques. In comparison to state-of-the-art FL approaches, experimental data show that RA-FKD delivers greater accuracy, decreases communication costs by up to 76%, and improves system efficiency. A cosine similarity loss KDC is introduced in knowledge distillation to improve the alignment between teacher and student models, enhancing knowledge transfer. Experimental evaluations on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets demonstrate that proposed framework achieving student test accuracy of 91.15% with reduction of 76.08% communication cost.</jats:p>

title: Knowledge Distillation and Explainability Analysis for Lightweight Retinal Disease Classification Using MultiEYE Fundus Images
abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Class imbalance and probabilistic prediction quality are important considerations in lightweight retinal classification. We evaluated whether knowledge distillation (KD) from a ConvNeXtV2-Base teacher improved an EfficientNet-B0 student in nine-class MultiEYE fundus classification. Methods: Exact-content screening quarantined 131 of 58,036 records because of exact-content duplication or label conflicts. Six prespecified seeds were evaluated in no-KD, label-smoothing, and KD arms (18 runs) under matched training conditions. Within the controlled experiment, TEST data were not used for training, hyperparameter tuning, checkpoint or model selection, or protocol modification. The primary endpoint was the KD−no-KD macro-F1 difference on decontaminated TEST (n = 11,573), assessed by paired image-level bootstrap (10,000 replicates). Grad-CAM and Grad-CAM++ were examined qualitatively using one deterministically selected case per class and six-seed consensus maps. Results: Mean macro-F1 was 0.593, 0.597, and 0.633 for no-KD, label smoothing, and KD. KD exceeded no-KD by 0.039 (95% CI, 0.025–0.053; p < 0.001), with positive paired differences in all six seeds, and label smoothing by 0.036 (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001); label smoothing did not differ from no-KD (Holm-adjusted p = 0.554). Class-wise F1 differences were non-negative across all nine classes, with six remaining significant after correction for multiple comparisons. The Brier score difference was −0.077 (95% CI, −0.081 to −0.072; Holm-adjusted p < 0.001), while ECE decreased descriptively from 0.171 to 0.084. Nine-class Grad-CAM and direct Grad-CAM++ consensus maps enabled qualitative no-KD versus KD comparison without establishing lesion-localization superiority. Conclusions: KD improved macro-F1 and lowered the Brier score while retaining the same EfficientNet-B0 student at inference. The evaluated label-smoothing configuration did not reproduce the macro-F1 gain; clinical superiority and external generalizability remain unestablished.</jats:p>

Cross-Resolution Knowledge Distillation for Low-Compute Fine-Grained Bird Classification
abstract: <jats:p>Fine-grained visual classification relies on subtle local cues and is highly sensitive to input resolution, yet practical deployment often constrains image size and inference cost. Existing low-resolution recognition methods often depend on additional network structures or complex training modules, limiting deployment simplicity. This study evaluates a simple cross-resolution knowledge distillation (KD) strategy under a fixed low-compute constraint. The teacher receives higher-resolution inputs to provide richer class-discriminative visual knowledge, whereas the student is trained at 160×160 and is the only model retained for deployment. Both networks use ResNet-18, allowing resolution-aware supervision to be studied without changing the inference architecture. On the CUB-200-2011 dataset, the 160×160 baseline achieved 66.01±0.53% test accuracy. The 224→160 KD configuration improved accuracy to 70.15±0.63%, while the final 384→160 configuration with T = 4 , α = 0.75 , and a 30-epoch cosine schedule reached 71.60±0.68% accuracy and 71.56±0.62% macro-F1. The results also show that a stronger teacher does not automatically produce a stronger student: transfer quality depends on the balance between teacher supervision strength and student optimization. These findings support cross-resolution KD as a practical way to recover fine-grained information during training while preserving low-resolution inference cost.</jats:p>

Cross-DATA: Cross-Data Attention Distillation for Lightweight Sound Classification with Limited Data
abstract: <jats:p>Using the UrbanSound8K dataset as a representative case, this study investigates how lightweight acoustic models can be trained with limited labeled data in resource-constrained environments. Because conventional knowledge distillation confines knowledge transfer to a single target dataset, it leaves the rich prior knowledge in external audio sources largely unused. We therefore propose Cross-DATA, a framework that treats a large-scale, general audio dataset such as FSD50K as an auxiliary knowledge source and integrates a newly designed Cross-data Attention Distillation mechanism. With mixed data batches as input, a powerful teacher model establishes inter-feature correlation patterns that the compact student network is encouraged to reproduce. In this way, the teacher's generic acoustic representations and discriminative capabilities can be transferred beyond the distribution of the target data, rather than being reduced to data augmentation or feature imitation. Experiments on UrbanSound8K show that the resulting student model surpasses traditional single-dataset distillation approaches in classification accuracy while using only about 4% of the teacher model's parameters and computational cost. Cross-DATA consequently alleviates the representational capacity deficit of lightweight models in small-data scenarios.</jats:p>

BioScaleML: A Lakehouse-Based Framework for,Large-Scale Biomedical Text Classification
abstract: <jats:p>Objective: The exponential growth of unstructured biomedical text across scientific literature, clinical narratives, and registries requires scalable, privacy-conscious informatics infrastructure. Existing solutions often rely heavily on managed cloud ecosystems, creating data governance, cost, and vendor lock-in challenges. This study presents BioScaleML, an open-source, local Lakehouse architecture designed to integrate end-to-end biomedical data management, scalable distributed processing, and reproducible machine learning (ML) pipelines within a controlled on-premises environment.,Methods: BioScaleML was engineered by coupling Apache Spark for distributed computation, Delta Lake for ACID-compliant transactional storage and schema enforcement, Hadoop for local persistence, and a PostgreSQL-backed Hive metastore for unified metadata management. The framework was evaluated across two curated biomedical text corpora totaling 49,118 documents (19,681 PubMed-style abstracts and 29,437 full-text article sections) annotated across major oncological categories (breast, lung, and prostate). Standardized Extract-Transform-Load (ETL) pipelines engineered TF-IDF feature representations, feeding reusable ML pipelines trained on local hardware.,Results: The integrated architecture enabled deterministic dataset versioning, robust schema governance, and end-to-end workflow execution on commodity infrastructure without cloud reliance. Baseline classification models—including Multinomial Logistic Regression, Linear Support Vector Machines, and Multinomial Naive Bayes—achieved consistent high-throughput classification across both corpora (reaching up to 90.6% accuracy), demonstrating that enterprise-grade data management and NLP processing can be achieved locally.,Conclusion: BioScaleML provides a practical, cost-effective blueprint for healthcare and research institutions seeking reproducible biomedical text analytics under strict data sovereignty constraints. By establishing a transaction-aware foundation, BioScaleML provides an extensible framework for scaling local informatics pipelines to advanced domain-specific language models and multi-modal clinical datasets.</jats:p>

title: Forecasting Fine-Tuning Break-Even Label Budgets in Text Classification from Frozen Embedding Geometry
abstract: Choosing between zero-shot inference and supervised fine-tuning is often a label-budget decision: practitioners want to know when additional supervision will make adaptation worthwhile. Existing comparisons usually determine this threshold only after training models across multiple data budgets, leaving no low-cost way to anticipate it. We test whether class separability in frozen sentence-embedding spaces can serve as a training-free, although label-dependent, predictor of this break-even. Because separability itself requires class labels, the experiment deliberately evaluates a strong-form geometric signal rather than an annotation-free deployment rule. In a prospectively prespecified study spanning 35 public English-language text-classification tasks and three sentence encoders, we related pre-adaptation separability to the label budget at which a supervised Transformer classifier first exceeded a fixed instruction-tuned zero-shot comparator. Silhouette-based separability did not satisfy the prespecified inferential and practical-utility criteria, and an alternative separability measure produced a different directional pattern. Many tasks also failed to reach break-even within the tested budget, producing substantial right censoring. Censoring-aware, heteroskedasticity-robust, and influence-oriented post hoc analyses did not materially change the interpretation. Frozen embedding separability alone is therefore not a sufficiently stable estimator of fine-tuning break-even in this comparison regime. These findings place an empirical boundary on a plausible geometric heuristic and suggest that useful forecasts will likely require comparator-aware information, local boundary structure, or early adaptation dynamics.

GLaDViT: interpretable gated fusion of frozen vision, text and layout features for document image classification
abstract: Classifying scanned pages by document type is a routing step in enterprisedocument processing. Layout-aware models reach high accuracy but rely onlarge-scale document pretraining and full fine-tuning, and seldom expose why adecision was made. We study a deliberately lightweight alternative, GLaDViT,which keeps CLIP and BERT encoders frozen, derives a layout descriptor fromTesseract hOCR word boxes, and trains only a gated fusion head. Because theclassifier is linear in the gated sum of modality embeddings, every class logitdecomposes exactly into per-modality terms, which yields an attribution that isfaithful to the computation by construction, unlike the gate weights alone. Ona label-corrected release of Tobacco-3482 (2737 pages, fixed 2186/272/279split), GLaDViT reaches \((93.7\pm0.4%)\) accuracy over three seeds (95% Wilsoninterval 90.2--96.0%), against 87.7% for the best single modality; addinglayout to vision and text contributes 2.8 accuracy points and gating a further1.1. The layout stream nevertheless receives at most about 10% of the gatemass, indicating that gate weights are mixing coefficients rather thanimportance scores. A triple InfoNCE alignment of the three streams, used as awarm-up on frozen features, lowers accuracy to 90.3%; we analyse this negativeresult. Code and hOCR tooling will be made publicly available.

Improved vision transformer for sports image classification via transfer learning and knowledge distillation
abstract: <jats:p>To address the challenges posed by complex visual characteristics in sports image classification, this study proposes an enhanced Vision Transformer (ViT) model built upon the Native Resolution ViT (NaViT) architecture. The principal innovations include replacing conventional single-layer feedforward networks with parallel feedforward networks and introducing an attention-guided distillation framework with input-dependent attention-weighted feature fusion, which adaptively regulates the contribution of frozen distillation features to the prediction pathway. The proposed approach leverages ImageNet-pretrained weights and performs domain-specific fine-tuning on sports datasets. Experimental results demonstrate substantial performance gains. On the multi-sport classification dataset, the proposed model achieves an accuracy of 0.9752 and a Macro-F1 score of 0.9753, outperforming the evaluated CNN benchmarks and ViT variants. For soccer match event classification, it achieves an accuracy of 0.9863 and a Macro-F1 score of 0.9718, while ranking first in the TOPSIS evaluation. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of integrating parallel feedforward processing, transfer learning, and distillation-guided feature fusion for sports image classification under complex visual conditions.</jats:p>

title: Unified Attention for Efficient Image Classification and Captioning
abstract: <jats:p>Transformers are the standard for visual representation learning and multimodal tasks like image captioning, but conventional multi-head attention relies on separate linear projections for queries, keys, and values, causing parameter redundancy and high computational cost. We propose Unified Attention, a parameter-efficient mechanism that reuses a single linear transformation across multiple attention passes. We instantiate this in Unified Vision Transformers (UViT) for image classification and Unified Transformers (UTR) for image captioning. Our approach reduces parameters per attention block by up to 75% while preserving essential structural dependencies and capturing consistent mappings between inputs and outputs. Experiments show that UTR improves image captioning metrics across multiple datasets, while UViT achieves competitive ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 83% with fewer parameters than baseline ViT. Unified Attention offers both a mapping-based interpretation of attention and a practical strategy for designing compact, efficient transformers for vision and multimodal tasks. The code for our experiments will be available on github upon acceptance.</jats:p>

title: KTCTPose: Efficient Coarse-to-Fine Human Pose Estimation via Knowledge-Token Self-Distillation
Multi-View Dual-Contrastive Graph Learning with Adaptive Agreement for Semi-Supervised Text Classification
abstract: Text classification with few labeled examples requires models that can effectively exploit unlabeled data while remaining lightweight. Graph-based approaches address this by modeling documents through their relations, but existing graph contrastive methods for text often rely on augmentations that alter semantic structure and are affected by unreliable false negatives. We propose Multi-View Dual-Contrastive Graph Learning (MDCGA), a framework that learns a shared document representation by integrating lexical, semantic, and keyword-based relational signals through enhanced dual contrastive objectives designed to reduce the impact of false negatives. Experiments on MR, Ohsumed, AG News, and R8 show that MDCGA achieves accuracies of 85.71%, 70.49%, 92.76%, and 97.40%, respectively. The approach demonstrates robustness in very low labeled settings, uses relatively few parameters, and shows limited sensitivity to hyperparameter choices.

Fidelity-Constrained Rule-Based Knowledge Distillation of Random Forests for Compact Breast Cancer Grade Classification
abstract: <jats:p>Breast cancer is a highly heterogeneous disease at the histopathological and molecular levels, and histological grade is a key prognostic indicator reflecting tumor biology. Although Random Forest models effectively capture nonlinear patterns in high-dimensional gene expression data, the decision logic of large tree ensembles remains difficult to inspect directly. This study proposes a knowledge-distillation framework that transfers the probabilistic decision behavior of a Random Forest teacher model to a compact, rule-based student model for distinguishing low- from high-histological-grade breast tumors using 20,385 gene-expression features from 1892 METABRIC samples, with clinical information used for sample matching and histological-grade label definition. Root-to-leaf decision paths extracted from the teacher were converted into a binary rule-activation matrix, followed by proximal group sparsification and fidelity-constrained Top-K rule selection. For the principal 400-tree teacher configuration, the student retained 65.0 ± 13.7 rules and achieved an ROC-AUC of 0.833 ± 0.023 and an average precision of 0.843 ± 0.019, while maintaining a raw teacher–student Pearson fidelity of 0.9607 ± 0.0112. As teacher capacity increased, the number of active decision paths increased substantially, whereas the selected rule budget remained within a comparatively narrow range and increased only modestly. The compact student also showed approximately 46% lower measured end-to-end inference latency and a 76% smaller serialized deployment size than the 400-tree teacher. Within the present METABRIC evaluation, these findings indicate that the structural complexity of a tree ensemble and the complexity required to approximate its probabilistic behavior need not scale proportionally, and that the proposed framework can provide a favorable trade-off among predictive performance, teacher fidelity, and deployment compactness.</jats:p>

title: Efficient Multivariate Time-Series Forecasting via Latency-Constrained Distillation and Dynamic Pruning
abstract: <jats:p>Multivariate time-series forecasting models often achieve improved prediction accuracy at the cost of increased model complexity and inference latency, limiting their deployment on resource-constrained computing platforms. In addition, lower parameter counts or theoretical computational costs do not necessarily lead to faster execution on actual hardware. To address this issue, we propose a Latency-Constrained Distillation and Dynamic Pruning (LCDP) framework for efficient multivariate time-series forecasting. LCDP introduces a latency-constrained adaptive optimization strategy that jointly considers forecasting loss, knowledge-distillation loss, local feature-alignment loss, and hardware inference latency during student-model training. Local feature-guided knowledge transfer is used to enhance the student model’s ability to capture fine-grained temporal patterns, while deployment-oriented dynamic structural pruning progressively adjusts the group-wise sparsity pattern of the student model according to latency feedback from the target hardware while retaining the original dense layer dimensions. Experiments on the ETTh1, ETTm1, and ETTm2 datasets using two CPU platforms show that LCDP achieves competitive forecasting accuracy with a lightweight student inference backbone containing 7336 active parameters and requiring 50,848 dense multiply-accumulate operations. The saved student checkpoint additionally contains 2080 parameters in a training-time feature-alignment projection that is not invoked during inference. LCDP provides an effective balance between forecasting accuracy and practical inference efficiency, demonstrating its potential for low-latency multivariate time-series forecasting on CPU-based resource-constrained platforms.</jats:p>

title: Sequential Shared-LoRA Adaptation of BERT for Text Classification: A Continual-Learning Baseline
abstract: <jats:p>Fine-tuning a pre-trained language model separately for every classification task is costly in computation and storage, and scales poorly when tasks arrive over time. Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) reduces this cost, but whether a single shared adapter can serve several classification tasks trained one after another remains underexplored. We study a frozen BERT-base backbone with one shared LoRA adapter in its self-attention layers and lightweight task-specific heads, trained sequentially on three tasks derived from the aclImdb movie-review corpus: binary sentiment, a rating-bucket task derived from the 1–10 review ratings, and a heuristic five-class genre task built from keyword rules, since the corpus has no genre metadata. The adapter and heads together comprise 302,602 of 109,784,842 parameters (0.2756%), cutting estimated storage for three tasks by 66.5% relative to per-task full fine-tuning. Each task peaks immediately after its own training stage (sentiment 88.6%, rating 89.1% against a 50% majority baseline, genre 57.2%). Sequential training, however, causes measurable forgetting: sentiment accuracy falls monotonically to 81.7% (forgetting score 0.0697) and rating accuracy from 89.1% to 83.5% (0.0550). These single-run results show that a compact shared adapter can support several related tasks while exposing interference under sequential adaptation, and they provide a reference accuracy–retention trade-off against which architecture-, regularization- and replay-based continual-learning mitigations can be evaluated.</jats:p>

title: SAS Multimetric Tribunal: Structural Classification of Hallucination in AI-Generated Text – What a Benchmark Design Can and Cannot Show
abstract:
<jats:p>Hallucination-detection systems are usually judged by a single headline metric, computed under a benchmark design that determines what that metric can show. This paper’s contribution is not a detection algorithm — structural coherence scoring is established — but a methodology for measuring exactly what a benchmark proves and what it does not, applied to the SAS Multimetric Tribunal: a seven-module, GPU-free structural classifier combining lexical, entity-mutation, curvature, and logical-inversion signals via a cascading multiplicative penalty (\(\kappa_{D} = 0.56\), \(\kappa_{R} = 0.15\)).

On a stratified 1,800-pair benchmark (HaluEval-Dialogue, HaluEval-QA, TruthfulQA), the tribunal reaches F1 = 98.99% with zero false positives under an A\(\rightarrow\)A identical-text sanity check — matched or exceeded by trivial baselines, including exact string matching (F1 = 100%). We report this explicitly: a benchmark that cannot fail on identical text cannot establish precision. Under a real negative control (R3: 127 valid paraphrase pairs), every method tested fails — the tribunal flags 126/127 as hallucinations (specificity 0.8%), matched by simple lexical baselines. No lexical-overlap method in our comparison distinguishes a valid paraphrase from a hallucination.

We also report, as direct ablations rather than argument, that multiplicative combination outperforms weighted averaging of the same seven modules by 87.97 F1 points, and that SourceTargetGuard’s measured contribution is 3 of 1,800 true positives (0.17% of recall). The tribunal’s contribution is not a solved precision problem: it is an auditable, per-module architecture on which a semantic-equivalence guard can be added and measured — something a single-metric baseline offers no place to attach. This revision also reports a forensic audit distinguishing an earlier version’s undocumented-but-reproducible metrics from a stale sub-count, corrected in response to independent peer review.</jats:p>

title: GeoDistillGaze: A knowledge distillation framework for efficient gaze target prediction
SmolVLA-Diff: efficient knowledge distillation for VLA models for vertical task deployment
abstract: <jats:p>This paper systematically compared the high performance π0 model with the high efficiency SmolVLA model. Real machine evaluation revealed that π<sub>0</sub> relying on its powerful flow matching action of generator and huge VLM model number, precision lead in vertical task; While SmolVLA through lightweight attention head and asynchronous reasoning stack, on delay, power consumption and anti-jamming advantage is obvious. In order to integrate the advantages of the two models, we innovatively propose an action knowledge distillation method at the output layer to transfer the action strategy knowledge of the π<sub>0</sub> model to SmolVLA, so that it can obtain similar performance improvement to the former with negligible additional overhead. This study provides an effective performance enhancement scheme for the efficient and practical deployment of the robot VLA model.</jats:p>
